blurb: Magma genesis, fragmentation, eruption columns, volcanic hazards, monitoring, climate, aviation ash and risk.

pics.alt: A huge grey eruption column rising above clouds and mountains, seen across a flat plain
pics.caption: The eruption column of Mount Pinatubo on 12 June 1991, three days before the climactic VEI 6 eruption, photographed from Clark Air Base. Forecasts and evacuations by PHIVOLCS and the USGS saved thousands of lives.
pics.title: Pinatubo91eruption plume.jpg

pics.alt: Satellite radar interferogram draped on 3-D terrain, with concentric colour fringes and a cone-shaped plot of uplift
pics.caption: InSAR interferogram (1995–2001) of the Three Sisters volcanic centre, Oregon: each colour cycle is 28.3 mm of line-of-sight range change. The lower panel shows the cumulative range change: a broad bulge of roughly 10–13 cm of uplift from magma intrusion at depth, detected with no eruption.
pics.title: InSAR Volcano.jpg
pics.artist: C. W. Wicks Jr. et al., USGS
